9	/-!
10	# Extension-uniformity: the free half WITNESSED, and the open half reduced to one scalar
11	
12	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` closes cluster-P items 1 and 3 over a *single* field `k`, and its
13	closing section says extension-uniformity splits into a free half and an open half.  That
14	section states the free half as a property of three **morphism classes**
15	(`baseChange_binders_stable`: `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and
16	`GeometricallyIrreducible` are each stable under base change).  That is true, and it is not
17	the same statement as "the vanishing theorem re-fires at the base-changed curve": a class
18	being stable under base change says nothing until some object is exhibited carrying the
19	base-changed instances, in the spelling the consuming theorem actually elaborates against.
20	
21	This file supplies the object.  `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean`)
22	is AJC's named base-changed curve `C_κ = C ×_{Spec k} Spec κ`, and it already carries
23	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral` as **named instances**.
24	One instance was missing from that stack — `GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is what the
25	`Ledger` curve statements bind — and `geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField` below adds
26	it.  With it, every curve-level statement of `FiberBound` applies to `C_κ` **by instance
27	synthesis alone**, at base field `κ`, with no new mathematics and no hypothesis on `κ/k`: not
28	finiteness, not separability, not perfectness.
29	
30	## What is proved here, and what is deliberately not
31	
32	* `vanishing_baseChangeField` / `riemannRoch_baseChangeField` — the **free half, witnessed**:
33	  a threshold `b(κ)` exists at `C_κ` for every `κ`, and exact Riemann–Roch holds above it with
34	  the base-changed genus `genus C_κ`.  This is the honest content of "the theorem re-fires per
35	  field", now stated at an object rather than about a class.
36	* `UniformVanishing` — the **open half, named as a definition** so that consumers can quantify
37	  over it and so that its exact quantifier order is inspectable: `∃ b, ∀ κ, ∀ D on C_κ, …`.
38	  The `b` is chosen **before** `κ`.  This is *not* proved here and this file does not claim it.
39	* `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` — the **reduction**: the open half
40	  follows from exactly **two** inputs, a uniform degree bound on a vanishing base divisor and
41	  base-field invariance of the genus.  Neither is proved here; both are named precisely.
42	
43	## What the constant actually decomposes into (correcting my own earlier account)
44	
45	`FiberBound`'s closing docstring located the obstruction in the constant: `b(κ)` is built from
46	`n₀(κ)`, a `Classical.choose` on a Noetherian stabilization re-run at each base field, and
47	nothing relates `n₀(κ)` to `n₀(k)`.  That describes the *proof*, not the *problem*.  The
48	threshold produced by `DegreeVanishing.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` is
49	
50	`b = deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪)`,
51	
52	and that existential is **monotone in `b`** (a `D` of degree `≥ b'` has degree `≥ b` whenever
53	`b ≤ b'`).  So `n₀` itself never has to transport: it suffices to bound `b(κ)` above by
54	something independent of `κ`.  Since `χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ` (`ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf`
55	composed with `GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`, both at `C_κ` — this is checked, not assumed),
56	
57	`b(κ) = deg_κ D₀(κ) + genus C_κ`,
58	
59	which exposes **two** `κ`-dependencies, not one:
60	
61	1. `genus C_κ` — a scalar, addressed by base-field invariance of the genus;
62	2. `deg_κ D₀(κ)` — the degree of the base divisor, where `D₀(κ) = n₀(κ) • F_κ`.  This is where
63	   the `Classical.choose` survives, and bounding it is *not* a corollary of (1).
64	
65	**A retraction.**  An earlier version of this docstring said the threshold "can be taken to be
66	`2g − 1`", which would have collapsed (2) into (1) and made the genus identity the whole
67	residue.  That is standard curve theory but it is **not available here**: `deg D ≥ 2g − 1 ⟹
68	H¹ = 0` goes through Serre duality, and there is **no Serre duality, canonical divisor or
69	dualizing sheaf anywhere in this workspace** — searched across AJC, AJCR and mathlib, which
70	has no Serre duality for curves at all.  So the reduction below carries both hypotheses.  I
71	had published the one-input version on the team thread before checking it; this is the
72	corrected form.
73	
74	## Where the two inputs stand (provenance, honestly)
75	
76	**Input (1), genus invariance: proved sorry-free next door, on a different carrier.**
77	`AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean` in
78	Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild proves `finrank_h1_baseField` (the `κ`-dimension of
79	`H¹(C_κ, 𝒪)` equals the `k`-dimension of `H¹(C, 𝒪)`, arbitrary field extension) and deduces
80	`genus_baseField`.  Its engine is termwise base change of the two-term Čech complex of an
81	affine two-cover plus right-exactness of `⊗` — not semicontinuity, not Mumford II.5.
82	
83	**The carrier question is settled, and favourably.**  AJCR states it at `baseChangeBundle C K`,
84	built from its own `overSpec`/`⊗` `Over`-tensor spelling, whereas AJC's `C_κ` is
85	`Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))))`.  Those agree by
86	`rfl` — **the whole bundled object, structure morphism included**, not merely the underlying
87	scheme.  AJCR's `⊗` is the monoidal product in `Over (Spec k)`, whose `tensorObj` *is* the
88	pullback and whose `snd` *is* `pullback.snd`, so the difference is notational indirection.
89	
90	Verified at *this* project's spelling rather than taken on report, with a negative control: the
91	same `rfl` with the pullback arguments swapped fails on a type mismatch, so the check is not
92	proving whatever it is handed.  Two caveats survive, and neither is cosmetic:
93	
94	* the verdict is defeq **at the object**.  A port that pushes it through a functor must re-run
95	  `rfl` there; a lane in this workspace shipped a false claim this week by carrying an
96	  object-level verdict across `Spec.map`.
97	* defeq of carriers is necessary, not sufficient.  The genus statements also bind AJCR's own
98	  curve-instance stack (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`) and its two-cover `curveCover`, and whether
99	  *those* land on AJC's `CurveBaseChange` instances is a separate measurement, not settled here.
100	
101	So the honest status of input (1) is: **reachable, cost not yet measured** — no longer "blocked on
102	a carrier mismatch", which is what I would have recorded had I stopped at the mismatch.  It stays
103	a hypothesis in the reduction below until the port is actually made, because an unmeasured port
104	is not an available theorem.
105	
106	**The AJC-native route to input (1), measured.**  Because the carriers agree, there is a second
107	option besides porting AJCR's file: assemble the identity from bricks AJC already owns.  What is
108	present, checked at HEAD:
109	
110	* a **cover on `C`**: `Adelic.LaurentChartData.pullbackSquare` (`Adelic/FinitenessP1.lean:439`)
111	  builds a `C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare` from the ℙ¹ chart data and any finite `π`, and
112	  `Ledger/MapToP1.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` supplies the `π` at AJC's curve;
113	* a **cover on `C_κ`**: `Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField` (`CurveBaseChange.lean:340`)
114	  transports it, since the first projection `C_κ ⟶ C` is affine;
115	* the **genus read on that cover**: `AffineCoverMVSquare.h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus`
116	  (`CohomologyKit.lean:582`) already says `h¹(𝒪_{C_κ})` on the base-changed cover *is*
117	  `genus C_κ`, and `h0_unit_baseChangeField_eq_one` gives `h⁰ = 1`.
118	
119	So AJC has both sides of the comparison expressed on transported covers; what is **missing** is
120	the comparison itself — the termwise base-change equivalence `Γ(C, V) ⊗_k κ ≃ Γ(C_κ, V_κ)` on
121	chart sections, which is what AJCR's `relSectionsBaseChange` supplies and what makes `h¹` agree
122	rather than merely both being defined.  That equivalence is the actual deliverable, on either
123	route.  Note the shape of the two projects' cover carriers differs — AJCR uses `AffineTwoCover`,
124	AJC `AffineCoverMVSquare` (and `AffineTwoCover` does not occur anywhere in AJC) — so a port
125	crosses a second carrier boundary that the `rfl` above does *not* cover.
126	
127	**Input (2), a uniform base-divisor degree bound: open, and not located in either project.**
128	It asks for one `d` with a vanishing `D₀` of degree `≤ d` over *every* `κ`.  Nothing in AJC or
129	AJCR bounds `n₀(κ)` uniformly; AJCR's analogue is a `Nat.find` per field
130	(`RiemannRoch/WindowLedger.lean`), and its `WindowFieldTransport.lean` transports vanishing
131	*facts* one field at a time precisely because the constant does not move.
132	
133	So `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` is a **conditional** result with one
134	antecedent that is proved-elsewhere-modulo-a-carrier and one that is genuinely open.
135	
136	## The three cluster-P statements, kept apart (unchanged discipline)
137	
138	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — closed at AJC's curve (`FiberBound`, three curve
139	   binders, nothing else).  This file changes nothing about it.
140	2. **Extension-uniformity** — free half now *witnessed* at `C_κ` (was: asserted of morphism
141	   classes); open half now *decomposed* into a genus identity plus a uniform base-divisor
142	   degree bound, with the second one named rather than folded into the first.  Still open.
143	3. **Global generation** — closed at AJC's curve by the dévissage route
144	   (`FiberBound.exists_bound_generated_of_isFinite_toP1`), independent of (1).  This file does
145	   not touch it; in particular nothing here makes generation uniform over extensions either.
146	-/

160	/-! ## §1. The missing instance
161	
162	`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` gives `C_κ` the named instances `IsProper`,
163	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral`.  The `Ledger` curve statements bind
164	`GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is the *irreducibility* half of geometric integrality and is
165	not recovered from it by synthesis.  Mathlib has the stability instance; this names it on the
166	`baseChangeField` spelling, exactly as its three siblings do. -/
167	
168	/-- **Geometric irreducibility is stable under the field base change.**  The instance that was
169	missing from the `CurveBaseChange` stack: with it, every curve-level statement of
170	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` applies to `C_κ` by synthesis, with no hypothesis on `κ/k`.
171	
172	Companion of `Scheme.geometricallyIntegral_hom_baseChangeField`, which is the *integral*
173	form; the `Ledger` layer binds the irreducible one. -/
174	instance Scheme.geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ]
175	    [Algebra k κ] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
176	    GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom :=
177	  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ ‹GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom›
178	
179	/-! ## §2. The free half, witnessed at `C_κ`
180	
181	Each theorem below is the corresponding `FiberBound` curve statement applied to
182	`Scheme.baseChangeField C κ`.  The proofs are one term each: that is the point — nothing has to
183	be redone at `C_κ`, and the reason nothing has to be redone is §1, not a stability claim about
184	morphism classes.
185	
186	The `letI`/`haveI` prologue is the standing `ChiCurve` idiom (see `FiberBound.lean` §Curve): it
187	makes the ambient structure morphism of `C_κ` definitionally its bundle map, so the smoothness
188	binder that `divisorSheaf` needs transfers by `inferInstanceAs`. -/
189	
190	section FreeHalf
191	
192	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
193	
194	/-- **Bounded `H¹` vanishing at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`** (the free half of
195	extension-uniformity, witnessed): a degree threshold exists over `κ`.
196	
197	The quantifier order is the whole content, and it is the *weak* one: `κ` comes first, then `b`.
198	Read `UniformVanishing` below for the strong order, which this does **not** give. -/
199	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
200	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
201	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
202	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
203	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
204	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
205	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
206	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
207	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) :=
208	  exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
209	
210	/-- **Exact Riemann–Roch at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`**:
211	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C_κ + deg_κ D` above a threshold over `κ`.
212	
213	Note the genus on the right is `genus C_κ`, taken over `κ`, **not** `genus C`.  Replacing it by
214	`genus C` is exactly the scalar identity §3 isolates, and it is not available here. -/
215	theorem riemannRoch_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
216	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
217	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
218	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
219	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
220	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
221	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
222	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
223	      (Sheaf.h0 ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) : ℤ)
224	        = 1 - genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) + CurveDivisor.deg κ D :=
225	  exists_bound_h0_eq_genus_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
226	
227	/-! ### The χ of `C_κ` is `1 − genus C_κ`
228	
229	The step that makes the decomposition of `b(κ)` in the module docstring a computation rather
230	than an estimate.  It is `ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf` at `C_κ` with the genus name corrected by
231	`GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`; both fire at `C_κ` only because of §1. -/
232	
233	/-- **`χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ`.**  Isolated because it is what pins the `κ`-dependence of
234	the vanishing threshold to the genus *and nothing else on the `χ` side*: the residual
235	`κ`-dependence of `b(κ)` sits entirely in `deg_κ D₀(κ)`. -/
236	theorem chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
237	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
238	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
239	    Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ)
240	      = 1 - (genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) : ℤ) := by
241	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
242	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
243	  rw [chi_moduleKSheaf (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ),
244	    ledgerGenus_eq_genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)]
245	
246	end FreeHalf
247	
248	/-! ## §3. The open half: named, and reduced to two explicit inputs
249	
250	`UniformVanishing` states the strong quantifier order — `b` before `κ` — as a definition, so
251	that a consumer can hypothesise it and so that the order is inspectable rather than buried in a
252	docstring.  It is **not proved**.
253	
254	`uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` reduces it to the two inputs the module
255	docstring names.  The reduction itself is unconditional: no vanishing hypothesis, no finiteness
256	supplied by the caller, and no appeal to Serre duality (which this workspace does not have). -/
257	
258	section OpenHalf
259	
260	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
261	
262	/-- **Extension-uniform bounded vanishing**, the statement.  One threshold `b`, chosen before
263	any field, serving every finite or infinite extension `κ/k` simultaneously.
264	
265	Contrast `vanishing_baseChangeField`, which is the same body with the quantifiers swapped:
266	there `κ` is fixed first and `b` may depend on it.  That one is a theorem; this one is open. -/
267	def UniformVanishing : Prop :=
268	  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
269	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
270	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
271	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
272	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
273	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
274	    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
275	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
276	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1)
277	
278	/-- **A uniform base-divisor datum**: one degree bound `d` such that over *every* extension
279	`κ/k` some divisor of degree `≤ d` already has vanishing `H¹`.
280	
281	This is input (2) of the reduction, and it is the genuinely open one.  Over a single `κ`,
282	`FiberBound.exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1` supplies such a `D₀` — namely `n₀ • F` —
283	but with no control of `deg_κ D₀` as `κ` varies, because `n₀(κ)` is chosen by a Noetherian
284	stabilization re-run at each base field. -/
285	def UniformBaseDivisor (d : ℤ) : Prop :=
286	  ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
287	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
288	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
289	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
290	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
291	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
292	    ∃ D₀ : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
293	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D₀) 1)
294	        ∧ CurveDivisor.deg κ D₀ ≤ d
295	
296	/-- **The reduction** (★): extension-uniform vanishing follows from a uniform base-divisor
297	degree bound together with base-field invariance of the genus, and the uniform threshold is
298	then simply `d + g`.
299	
300	Both hypotheses are needed and neither implies the other; see the module docstring for where
301	each stands.  The proof is the monotonicity observation and nothing more: the explicit bound of
302	`DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` at `C_κ` is
303	`deg_κ D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = deg_κ D₀ + genus C_κ ≤ d + g`, so a `D` of degree `≥ d + g`
304	clears it. -/
305	theorem uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant {d : ℤ} {g : ℕ}
306	    (hbase : UniformBaseDivisor C d)
307	    (hgenus : ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
308	      genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) = g) :
309	    UniformVanishing C := by
310	  refine ⟨d + (g : ℤ), fun κ _ _ => ?_⟩
311	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
312	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
313	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
314	      ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
315	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
316	  intro D hD
317	  obtain ⟨D₀, hvan, hdeg⟩ := hbase κ
318	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ) = 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
319	    rw [chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField C κ, hgenus κ]
320	  refine subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge κ hvan D ?_
321	  rw [hchi]
322	  omega
323	
324	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
325	/-- The uniform statement is **strictly stronger** than the per-field one, in the only sense
326	that can be stated without proving either: it implies the per-field conclusion at every `κ`.
327	Recorded so that a consumer cannot mistake `vanishing_baseChangeField` for it.
328	
329	The `omit [IsProper C.hom]` is informative rather than cosmetic: the implication is pure
330	quantifier weakening — instantiate the single `b` at each `κ` — so it needs no properness, and
331	the linter caught that.  It confirms the two statements differ *only* in quantifier order, with
332	no geometry in between. -/
333	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField_of_uniformVanishing (h : UniformVanishing C)
334	    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
335	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
336	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
337	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
338	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
339	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
340	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
341	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
342	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) := by
343	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := h
344	  exact ⟨b, hb κ⟩
345	
346	end OpenHalf
347	
348	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## §2. The base-changed curve and its named curve-package instances -/

section BaseChangeField

variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ]

/-- **The base change of a `k`-scheme `C` along a field extension `κ/k`**:
`C_κ := C ×_{Spec k} Spec κ`, as an object of `Over (Spec κ)` via the second
projection. The named carrier of the Λ-stability instances below (instances
are keyed on this definitional spelling). -/
noncomputable def baseChangeField : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
  Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))))

/-- Smoothness of relative dimension `1` is stable under the field base change
(`smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange`, extraction of the inline
recipe at `RiemannRoch/Adelic/NonconstantToP1.lean:986-989`). -/
instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_hom_baseChangeField
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeField C κ).hom :=
  haveI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ ‹SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom›

/-- Properness is stable under the field base change (Mathlib
`IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange`). -/
instance isProper_hom_baseChangeField [IsProper C.hom] :
    IsProper (baseChangeField C κ).hom :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ ‹IsProper C.hom›

/-- Geometric integrality is stable under the field base change. **Audit item
6** (see the module docstring): the in-tree `GeometricallyIntegral` is the
Mathlib class "every field-valued base change of `f` has integral total
space", and its stability under arbitrary base change — a fortiori under the
field extension `φ : Spec κ ⟶ Spec k`, by transitivity of base change — is
already provided by Mathlib
(`MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange @GeometricallyIntegral`); this
named instance re-exports it keyed on the `baseChangeField` spelling. -/
instance geometricallyIntegral_hom_baseChangeField [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    GeometricallyIntegral (baseChangeField C κ).hom :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ ‹GeometricallyIntegral C.hom›

/-- **A rational point base-changes**: a section `σ` of `C.hom` lifts to the
section `pullback.lift (φ ≫ σ) (𝟙 _)` of the base-changed structure morphism
(pattern `IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso`, `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`,
specialised to the section rather than the group structure). -/
instance hasRationalPoint_baseChangeField [HasRationalPoint C] :
    HasRationalPoint (baseChangeField C κ) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨σ, hσ⟩⟩ := HasRationalPoint.nonempty_section (C := C)
  refine ⟨⟨⟨pullback.lift (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ)) ≫ σ) (𝟙 _) ?_, ?_⟩⟩⟩
  · rw [Category.assoc, hσ, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
  · exact pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

/-- The total space of the base-changed curve is integral (named substrate
instance for the adelic gate `Scheme.instIsConstantField` on `C_κ`). -/
instance isIntegral_left_baseChangeField [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    IsIntegral (baseChangeField C κ).left :=
  isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyIntegral (baseChangeField C κ)

/-- The total space of the base-changed curve is locally noetherian (named
substrate instance for the adelic gate `Scheme.instIsConstantField` on `C_κ`). -/
instance isLocallyNoetherian_left_baseChangeField [IsProper C.hom] :
    IsLocallyNoetherian (baseChangeField C κ).left :=
  isLocallyNoetherian_left_of_locallyOfFiniteType (baseChangeField C κ)

/-- The total space of the base-changed curve is regular in codimension one
(named substrate instance for the adelic gate `Scheme.instIsConstantField` on
`C_κ`; specialisation of the arbitrary-field curve regularity
`isRegularInCodimensionOne_left_of_curve`). -/
instance isRegularInCodimensionOne_left_baseChangeField
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne (baseChangeField C κ).left :=
  isRegularInCodimensionOne_left_of_curve (baseChangeField C κ)

end BaseChangeField

/-! ## §3. Base change of a 2-affine Mayer–Vietoris cover square -/

section CoverBaseChange

variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ]

/-- The first projection `C_κ ⟶ C` of the field base change is an affine
morphism: it is the base change of the affine `Spec κ ⟶ Spec k` (pattern
`isAffineHom_p1BaseChange_fst`, `Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`). -/
instance isAffineHom_baseChangeField_fst :
    IsAffineHom (pullback.fst C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ)))) :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_fst (P := @IsAffineHom) C.hom
    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ)))
    (inferInstance : IsAffineHom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))))

variable {C}

/-- **A 2-affine Mayer–Vietoris cover square base-changes along a field
extension**: the preimage (`AffineCoverMVSquare.preimage`,
`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`) of a bundled 2-affine cover of `C` under the
affine first projection `C_κ ⟶ C`. Charts are identified by
`baseChangeField_U₁`/`baseChangeField_U₂`. Companion of
`AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeSpecOver` (`Picard/FinitePresentationFunctor.lean`),
which is keyed on the `specOver k A` base shape; this one is keyed on the raw
`Spec.map (algebraMap k κ)` spelling. -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.AffineCoverMVSquare :=
  show (pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ)))).AffineCoverMVSquare from
    S.preimage (pullback.fst C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))))

/-- Chart identification for the base-changed cover square: the first chart is
the preimage of the first chart. -/
@[simp] lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField_U₁ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ =
      pullback.fst C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))) ⁻¹ᵁ S.U₁ :=
  rfl

/-- Chart identification for the base-changed cover square: the second chart is
the preimage of the second chart. -/
@[simp] lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField_U₂ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ =
      pullback.fst C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))) ⁻¹ᵁ S.U₂ :=
  rfl

end CoverBaseChange

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.ExtensionUniformity

universe u
open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry Scheme

namespace Probe10
variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]

-- NON-VACUITY: given ONE closed point with positive residue degree, degrees are unbounded,
-- so a bound `b` is never trivially satisfied by an empty degree half-space.
theorem deg_unbounded {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
    (hpos : 0 < X.residueDeg K x) (b : ℤ) :
    ∃ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.single hx (max b 0), ?_⟩
  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx]
  have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hpos
  have hb : b ≤ max b 0 := le_max_left _ _
  have h0 : (0:ℤ) ≤ max b 0 := le_max_right _ _
  calc b ≤ max b 0 := hb
    _ = max b 0 * 1 := by ring
    _ ≤ max b 0 * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 h0

end Probe10
EOF

asserted here. -/

  have h0 : (0 : ℤ) ≤ max b 0 := le_max_right _ _
